decision_rule: Replace a plastic product only after defining the service, safety requirements, lifetime, geography, collection system, and counterfactual. Prevention and reuse usually deserve evaluation before one-for-one material substitution.
priority_order: Reduce material and hazardous constituents without impairing the service
Deliver the service through reuse, refill, repair, sharing, or concentration
Use high-quality closed-loop recycling where collection and markets exist
Substitute material only after functional-unit life-cycle assessment
Use controlled compostables only where they improve organics collection and compatible infrastructure exists

preferred_changes: durable bag reuse with measured trip count
paper or cellulose only where moisture and reuse requirements permit
application_pathways.do_not_claim: A material is better from its name alone.
Single-use glass or metal automatically saves water.

preferred_changes: uncoated fiber for suitable dry short-contact uses
conditional_materials: certified compostable polymer in closed organics systems
application_pathways.do_not_claim: Compostable means it will decompose in the environment.

preferred_changes: sell suitable goods loose or in bulk
standardize reusable transport and retail containers
use cellulose or seaweed coatings only after shelf-life testing
application_pathways.do_not_claim: Packaging water can be evaluated without the protected food.

preferred_changes: natural or regenerated cellulosic fibers where full impacts are lower
evaluate PE, PP, EVA, silicone, thermoplastic elastomers, or non-PVC tubing by clinical function
application_pathways.do_not_claim: A blanket medical substitution is safe without device-specific validation.

preferred_changes: application-specific ductile iron, copper, clay, concrete, wood, or composite comparison
application_pathways.do_not_claim: Removing long-lived pipe necessarily reduces total water use or leakage.

preferred_changes: collection only where a stable end market exists
application_pathways.do_not_claim: Replacing protective foam is beneficial if product damage rises materially.

preferred_changes: cellulose, mineral wool, wood fiber, cork, or other systems after fire, moisture, thermal, and durability testing
application_pathways.do_not_claim: Embodied impact may be assessed without operational building energy.
Immediate elimination is appropriate where no validated safe replacement exists.

burden_shifting_evidence.finding: A 2024 comparative greenhouse-gas study found plastic lower in 15 of 16 modeled applications. This does not prove plastic is preferable on water, toxicity, litter, or biodiversity; it proves that a replacement decision must retain function and examine multiple impacts.
